cohort: 826 periviable singleton infants born between 22 0/7 and 25 6/7 weeks of gestation in Taiwan between 2010 and 2016
finding: While cesarean delivery was associated with a decreased risk of IVH in periviable singleton births, it did not improve rates of severe IVH, mortality, or neurodevelopment at 2 years of age.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a decreased risk of IVH overall, and with better survival without neurodevelopmental impairment in the small-for-gestational age subgroup.
